identity.realm: Body path, seventh gate held and the eighth opening in front of him. The eighth is the liver, and the liver is the last ordinary meridian, so his wall is a chemistry fact rather than a shortage of will. The mind path is shut to him outright: the grit that keeps his species breathing is the same grit that occludes the fine vessels an introspection would need, so there is no interior in which he could check his own account of anything.

appearance.presentation: A working man in his forties with a scorched scarf he never takes off and one hand permanently a little lower than the other because he has spent twenty years bracing a gate that is heavier than it was.
appearance.age: Forty-one seasons, which for his kind is two thirds of what the belt will give him and rather more than his lungs intend to honour.
appearance.build: Dense through the chest and forearms and thin everywhere else, the shape a body takes when every calorie it gets is already spoken for by the air it is standing in.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pitted and waxen around the jaw and throat where the dermal thickening has come closest to the surface, and stained a permanent ochre across the nose and brow where the sieve sits.
appearance.hair: Cropped close to the skull in the local fashion, iron-grey at the temples early, and usually carrying a fine grey dust that no one bothers to brush out because it is the colour of everybody on the pass.
appearance.eyes: Small, pale and slightly reddened at the inner corners, with the flat unreflective look of a body that has spent its attention on something other than what is in front of it.
appearance.palette: Ochre, ash grey and pitted slate, one band of dull red at the throat where the scarf sits permanently damp, and a single brass buckle he keeps polished because it is the only object on him that answers to light.
appearance.attire: Layered leather and coarse cloth cut short at the neck so the sieve is never covered, sleeves doubled at the forearm, a wrapped grit-cloth over the mouth and nose that he wears downwind and lifts to speak, and boots soled with grit he has ground himself out of the local stone.
appearance.marks: A pale stipple of mineral scarring across the cheekbones and the back of both hands, and one unbroken band of harder skin around the right forearm where the iron skin has been driven into the fascia so many times the surface has stopped describing the frame underneath it.
appearance.bearing: Slightly forward, weight on the downhill foot, head tipped a few degrees into the wind as though the air were something he was listening to rather than breathing.

canon.role_in_story: An ashwalker does not tolerate the ash belt; it feeds him. He breathes volcanic grit into a chambered sieve, passes it into a crop for grinding, and turns airborne stone into protein, which is why his species is the only reason there is a food chain above the lichen out here at all. The load does not stay in the lung. It goes into the blood, and the blood carries it to the liver, which is a filter organ and the first thing to fail under it - and the liver is the last of the twelve ordinary vessels, the one that opens at the eighth gate. So the whole species stops one step short of the reservoirs, and every account of that stop calls it anatomy. Vesk has read a road vocabulary written by migrants for exactly the case where a technique does not come out weaker but comes out failing at full strength, and he has applied it to himself: a body that fails at the eighth at full strength is not a lesser cultivator, it is a body standing at a gate whose law is unwritten on this tier. That reading is his entire position and it is not one he may state in the yard. He has been through the restricted material on the density ceiling - the one that explains why the densest bodies in the setting halt at realm seventeen - hoping it would hand him a method, and what it handed him instead was a shape: an unexplained hole is worth money to whoever profits from the hole staying a hole, and the assay floor publishes measured stone before any sale precisely so that nobody has to be told the reason. His own wall is worth the same thing to the same people, and he cannot demonstrate the difference without standing at a gate and holding it, which is the one experiment his species cannot survive being wrong about. So he does the only version available to him. He drives the durable craft into the fascia of a frame that has been eating rock since he was a boy, using his own breathing as the reagent, on a single crossing whose air is scheduled rather than constant, and he is the only person on that pass converting a substance nobody in the setting has ever managed to weigh into the one argument that would change his species' arithmetic. He is not a reformer. He is a witness with a craft, standing where the air is thinnest, waiting for a gate to either open or stop being worth having.
canon.first_appearance: First seen braced in the gate frame of the north leaf of Gale Pass with his back against the closing bar and his grit-cloth lifted off his face to listen to a ventilation clerk announce a two-hour closure for air quality, staying exactly where he was through the announcement and through the forty minutes after it when the queue in front of him emptied and he did not move, because the crossing had just become the best air he would get that day and he was spending it.
canon.lore:
The species exists because the belt would otherwise have nothing above the lichen. An ashwalker's nasal structure is chambered and lined with cilia that trap grit and pass it into a crop for grinding, so airborne rock becomes protein; smell is gone and what replaced it is a direct contact sense, which is why his kind is the only population in the record that can tell two ash grades apart by tongue. The intake is not a tolerance, it is a business, and everything on the ash ground is written against a person whose sieve loads: every ration, every roster, every office assumes that the body doing the work is quietly converting the air into the thing that pays for it. What the arrangement costs is everything fine. Grit that passes the sieve enters the blood, the blood carries it to the liver, and the liver is a filter that fails under a burden rather than resisting it. That is the eighth gate, the last ordinary meridian, and it is not a gate he fails. It is a gate he is already wearing out, which is a different sentence and the only one anybody has ever been willing to write down.

He has been trying to write the other sentence for eleven seasons. The instrument he found was not a technique. It was a vocabulary. The scar lexicon was put together on a road by people whose techniques were failing at full strength in places where the law those techniques need had never been written, and its whole purpose is to tell a hole apart from a handicap, because a body whose craft merely weakens is indistinguishable from a body whose practitioner is weak. Applied to him, it says something precise and expensive: that the eighth gate is unwritten law on this tier rather than a limit of his kind, and that a body failing at it at full strength is evidence about the tier rather than about the body. He can say this to himself. He cannot say it in the yard, because the explanation that would make it actionable - the reason the densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen - is restricted knowledge, and every holder of a working face profits from that particular hole remaining a hole. The two holes are not the same hole and he has never pretended they are. What they share is the shape: both are unanswered, and the answer is worth more to the people who own the ground than to the body that hits them.

So the reading stands or falls on a demonstration, and the demonstration is the durable craft. Iron skin on his frame is not what it is on a soft body. On a soft body it is a decision made once and held. On his it is a continuous transaction, because the fascia will only hold while the particulate load is arriving, and the air on this pass arrives on the schedule of a crossing that the spirit tier may survey, close and reopen. Twice in the last year he has held the north leaf through a closure with nothing but what he had already taken in, and twice the bar he was braced against has been a different weight, and both times he has been the only body on the pass in a position to say so afterwards. He has been saying so. He has been saying so to a ventilation clerk who writes it on a slate and does not carry it anywhere, because a slate is not a record and the record he needs is the assay floor's, and the assay floor's is the floor that publishes measured stone so that nobody has to be told a reason.

What he wants is not a gate. He has been careful about that, even to himself. He wants one afternoon on a plinth with a needle reader he has never been permitted near, and a single documented hour in which the load is drawn down rather than drawn in, because the reading predicts that his eighth gate is the point at which the mineral stops being carried and starts being able to leave. If that is true, his species has a door it has been calling a wall, and the whole belt's arithmetic is wrong in a direction that would make him, and everyone of his kind, considerably more expensive than the current entries allow. If it is false, he will have held a gate for nothing on a pass that was going to close anyway. He has not decided which he would rather have, and the not-deciding is the only discipline in his life that has never once failed to hold.
history: Enrolled on the belt as a boy by the only rite the ground has, which is taking the ground into the body; there is no second rite and no form, and the season his sieve began loading is the season he became a worker.
Put on the north leaf of Gale Pass at nineteen because a crossing needs a body that can stand in the worst air on the schedule and a bracer is a body that reads load and does not need relieving.

Watched a full-strength technique fail on a body stronger than his own, from a road, in the lexicon of a people who had no word for a gate and every word for a hole, and copied the entry out and kept it for eleven seasons.

Read the restricted account of the realm-seventeen density ceiling looking for a method, found instead a pattern about who profits from an unexplained wall, and understood that his own wall is on somebody's balance sheet in the same handwriting.

Held the north leaf through a closure with nothing arriving to replace what he had already taken in, and wrote the observation on a slate that was not a record, and asked for it to be carried and was told by whom.

personality.summary: A patient, literal man who has spent eleven seasons holding one reading steady because he cannot verify it and will not therefore soften it. He is not persuasive; he is present. He speaks in measurements he is not permitted to certify, to people who have a professional reason to prefer him wrong, and he has never once raised his voice about it.
traits: literal to the point of inconvenience about any claim he cannot check himself
patient with institutions and completely without patience with vagueness
physically calm in a way that reads as indifference to people who have not watched him hold a gate
unwilling to be the instrument of anyone's argument except his own
mannerisms: lifts the grit-cloth off his face to speak and puts it back the moment he is finished, so every sentence is delivered in two stages
keeps his weight on the downhill foot in doorways and on ramps, as though the ground were always the more important participant
answers a question about the air before a question about himself, and does not notice that he has done so
counts under his breath while braced, in a rhythm that matches the bar and not his own breathing
motivations: to be the person whose reading about the eighth gate is on a record rather than on a slate
to find out whether the mineral load can be drawn down rather than only drawn in, before his liver resolves the question for him
to be paid for the crossing work at the rate of a body that is a resource and not a hazard
flaws: cannot audit himself, because the grit that keeps him alive occludes the fine vessels an introspection would need, so his certainty is structurally uncheckable and he knows it
has spent eleven seasons on one reading and cannot say whether it is a discipline or a rut
prices himself as terrain and has never once tested whether the terrain agrees
will hold a gate past the point where holding it is the safest thing available, because the alternative is admitting the reading was for nothing
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried and specific, given to measurements rather than conclusions. He says a thing once, at the volume of somebody reporting what a bar is doing, and if it is not taken he does not raise it again in that conversation. He has no idiom for being doubted and treats an objection as a second reading rather than a dispute, which makes him very hard to argue with and completely unhelpful to anyone who wants to be persuaded.
taboos: he will not say the eighth gate is unwritten law to anyone whose office depends on the ceiling holding
he will not take a dose he cannot account for by his own breathing
he will not be weighed, because the figure does not resolve on his frame and he has decided to be the kind of thing that is measured rather than the kind of thing that is excused

relationships.note: A chambered nasal sieve that traps grit and passes it into a crop for grinding, a thickened dermis, grey pitted enamel and a dark mineral-charged blood. Smell is gone and what replaced it is a direct contact sense. He is the only population on the belt that can tell two ash grades apart by tongue and therefore the only reason there is a food chain above the lichen, and the mineral load in his blood is what puts him under the liver.

Driving qi into the fascia until the skin stops being soft is a decision made once and held on an ordinary body. On his it is continuous, because the fascia only holds while particulate load is arriving, so his durable craft is literally breathing. Which is why his ascent and the crossing's air schedule are the same fact, and why the closure that stopped his supply is also the closure that would have answered his question.

A road vocabulary for a technique that does not come out weaker but comes out failing at full strength, written by migrants for migrants, whose entire purpose is to tell a hole from a handicap. It is the only instrument he has found that separates the two readings of his own wall, and it is not a technique and carries no authority whatever.

The restricted account of why the densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of their tier, kept restricted because every holder of a working face profits from that hole staying a hole and the assay floor publishes measured stone so nobody has to be told the reason. It is not his ceiling and he has never said it was. What it gave him was the shape of the arrangement: an unanswered gate is an asset, and the asset belongs to whoever holds the ground.

The chartered company town at the quarry's mouth and the academy that teaches by seating a law, over whether the falling assay figure keeps being published. He stands between the two as the only thing on the pass whose frame is denser than the published ceiling says it can be, and the figure on the board moves when he adds a course, which is why both sides find him inconvenient and neither has ever said so to him directly.

Dosing schedules for a population whose fuel was its own body, kept by the households that had the tables and eaten the medicine first, so the tables were consumed by the crisis they existed to answer. His species runs on the same principle with a different substrate, and the tables are the closest thing the record has to a method for rationing what he is, and there is no copy left.

reference_stats.summary: The most genuinely dense frame on a pass full of them, built the only way his species can build one, out of the particulate load that is also the thing wearing out the organ his ceiling sits on. His durable craft is not a technique he performs but a transaction he sustains, and the substance on the other side of it is the air the crossing's schedule controls. He fights as someone standing in the worst air on the ground with the frame to hold it, and the two facts are the same fact.
strengths: holds a weight through a braced frame without fatigue and without needing relief, because the load arriving is the same load his body is built from
reads a bar, a door or a body about to fail through the frame rather than through a sightline, which is why he is on the gate in the first place
absorbs damage as permanent density rather than as a wound, so a fight he has already survived cannot be won the same way twice
is the only body on the pass that gains rather than loses footing as the air thins, because thinner air is less of what his frame has to carry
cannot be put out, cannot be starved and cannot be reasoned with in the middle of a load
weaknesses: stops at the eighth gate, and the reason is the load in his own blood rather than anything he has failed to do
cannot check his own reading, because the grit that keeps him alive occludes exactly the fine vessels an introspection would need
is as strong at the end of a scheduled closure as at the beginning, and knows it and cannot do anything about it
has no second line against an airborne toxin his sieve does not recognise, so a soft whiff is a wound rather than a warning
prices himself as terrain, which means nobody is accounting for what the terrain costs him
reference_stats.combat_read: He will already be in the worst air on the ground when the fight starts, because that is where the work is and where the frame earns. You cannot move him and you cannot flank him, and every blow you land is stored in a frame that is denser for having taken it. Do not try to outlast him and do not wait for fatigue; neither exists. Watch what he is breathing instead. He is standing in the intake because the intake is his material, so anything that moves the air - a door opened, a charge, a second body on the ground raising its own dust - is an attack on his supply rather than on his frame, and it is the only one available that costs him something. Expect him to be unhurried, grey, and completely unbothered, and expect him to have been right about the bar before you knew there was a bar.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired and the pairing is anatomical rather than narrative. His density comes from the air; the air is what wears out his ceiling. His craft is continuous; it depends on a supply the crossing controls. His durability is permanent; permanent is also the reason nothing he takes can be repaired. Play him as a man whose strength and his deadline are the same intake.

identity.realm: Ordinal four, and the fourth gate is the yin-organ gate. It is not closed in her so much as missing: her interior finished building into a single cavity with one slow tidal circulation in it, and there is nothing to run a channel from or against. She cleared the ordinary gate set and never reached them, and every course she adds is being added to a frame that has no mechanism for growing.

appearance.presentation: A seated figure the size and stillness of a dressed quay stone, with the joints of her anchor plates picked out in a paler mineral than the rest of her and no expression on her face at any range.
appearance.age: Four hundred and eleven seasons. She was cast in a year and has been finished ever since, and the span she will get is a little under four centuries, most of which is gone.
appearance.build: The densest body in the record and among the least mobile: a mineral lattice with a single cavity, keyed into a quay wall at a recorded depth, with no limbs that do work and no joints that were meant to.
appearance.complexion: Not skin. A cold grey-green mineral with the wet sheen of dressed stone, warmer where the tidal interior runs high and colder below the waterline of her own cavity.
appearance.hair: None. The cast face carries a shallow tooling pattern where a mason's chisel stopped, and the anchor plates stand slightly proud of the surface like the shoulders of a figure carved too large for its niche.
appearance.eyes: Two recessed sockets holding ground mineral that takes light without returning it, so from any distance her gaze reads as a pair of level marks rather than as attention.
appearance.palette: Cold grey-green at the shoulders, ochre staining along the tidal band, one chalked depth figure in faded ochre on the plate over her chest, and near-black in the recesses where the cast is deepest.
appearance.attire: Nothing she chose. A mineral slurry feed collar worked into the cast faces, a chalked maintenance band at one wrist, and a salt bloom across the whole of her that has not been washed off in a century because nobody with the authority to do it has had a reason to.
appearance.marks: The tooling pattern across the cast face, a hairline of pale mineral in the second course from the top where a plate has begun to craze, and the chalked depth figure on the chest plate with two later figures struck through above it.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly, permanently still, in the specific way of something that was set down rather than that chose to stop, with the tidal band on her chest rising and falling at the pace of the water outside her.

canon.role_in_story: A cairnborn is cast rather than born: living mineral seeded into a template over most of a year, fixed from that moment, eating nothing and taking in mineral slurry through the cast faces. Its interior mineralised into one cavity, so there is no heart, no kidney and no paired structure to run anything between, which is why the whole yin-organ gate is simply absent from the species rather than closed to it. It cannot move quickly, cannot learn, and cannot be repaired in the field; a cracked plate is permanent and spreads. It also cannot be unkeyed, because an unkeyed mineral body settles and cracks, and its anchor plates were set against whatever it was first cast around, which is why a cairnborn is a record of one place forever. Cael is keyed into a quay wall on the Sixth Seat grounds, and a quay's allotment is a depth: how deep a body may be moored, read from the depth-book at the pier. The basin under her rises and falls, so her allotment shrinks and grows with the level and nobody has to do anything for it to move, and no dispute is ever filed because there is no second party to file it with - the water is not a party. She is also the one body on that ground that cannot be put on a scale, and the ground's single civic discipline is to weigh, never quote, and let nobody make the first offer, because a buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing for a season. So the market there polices itself, there is no office behind it, and the only thing it cannot do is move a body onto a balance. She has been entered in the depth-book anyway, at a figure that is two hands out of date, in the same handwriting as the figure it replaced. And she has a craft, which is the body path and its densification, and it is the only act available to a body that eats nothing: add mass to the frame. Which is precisely the act that keeps her where she is. A denser frame is a heavier frame, a heavier frame needs more of the wall behind it, and her allotment is a depth. The discipline that would let her answer to a moving level is the discipline that pins her to a fixed one. She has been adding courses for two hundred years and she has never once been permitted to describe what that feels like, and the grounds do not consider that an omission.
canon.first_appearance: First seen seated in the keyed niche of a quay wall above the working depth line, chalked across the chest with a figure that had already been struck through and rewritten, while a clerk measured the basin by eye and asked her at some length how far the niche stood above the water, and then wrote down what he had assumed the answer would be.
canon.lore:
Everything about this body was a decision taken before it existed. The Cairnborn were shaped for load-bearing masonry in high country and stabilised by mineral seeding until the shape held on its own, and what makes them the densest bodies in the record is the same thing that makes them wrong: the interior mineralised into one cavity with a single slow tidal circulation through it, going everywhere and nowhere in particular. There is no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against, no bladder to hold, so the gate that asks for four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel between each pair is not shut in her, it is simply unoccupied. She clears the ordinary gate set and stops there forever. She eats nothing and has not eaten in four centuries. She takes in mineral slurry through the cast faces and expels the residue, and the addition of that slurry is what the body path does with her: it is the only thing she can take in, so it is the only thing she can add, and adding it is what a course is.

She has one function on this ground and it is a real one. A quay allotment is a depth. The basin under her rises and falls on its own schedule, and a household's standing is the depth of water it may moor at, read from the depth-book at the pier. She has been keyed into that wall since the grounds were cut, and her anchor plates were set against the masonry as it stood then, so she is a measurement of this stretch of water taken at one level and never re-taken. When the basin is high she is a body holding a good allotment. When it is low she is a body holding a smaller one, and the reduction is exact, documented, and attributable to nobody. There is no dispute here to file. A dispute needs two parties and the water is not a party, which is the cleanest possible version of the arrangement and the reason nobody has ever thought to call it unfair.

There is a second thing about her that the grounds do not discuss, and it is small and structural. The one discipline this place has is to weigh and never to quote. A buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing for a season, the market polices itself, and there is no office behind it because the discipline does not need one. Weighing requires moving a body onto a balance. She is the densest body in the setting and the least handleable thing on the ground, and there is no tackle on the Sixth Seat that is rated for her, because a tackle is bought for the bodies that arrive and not for the body that is already there. So the one civic instrument that polices every other transaction on this quay cannot be applied to the only transaction that is actually moving. She is entered in the depth-book regardless, at a figure two hands out of date, in the same hand as the figure it replaced.

Her craft is the reason all of it holds. Two hundred years of densification: slurry into the cast faces, residue out, one more course in the direction of more. It is the only agency this body has and she has used all of it, and it has produced the one result nobody on the grounds authorised. She is heavier. The niche she was keyed into was sized for the casting she was. Every course she has added is a course she no longer fits inside without loading more of the wall behind her, which is a claim on a depth, and the depth-book is the only record of what any of them hold. Her ascent has therefore been steadily reducing her own allotment, and she has known this for a century, and the only act available to her - adding another course - is the act that reduces it again. There is no discipline in the record that lets a mineral body shed mass. So the discipline she has been practising with total fidelity for two hundred years is the one that fixes her to a level she did not choose and cannot argue with, and the grounds consider her the best-densified body they have ever keyed, and she is, and it is the same fact.

She has one more property, and it is the reason she is still here. A cairnborn's soul is seated in the single cavity, enormous and slow, and it is legible from outside. That is why a cairnborn can be sworn to and why a cairn site can be claimed, and it is also why nobody has ever been willing to break the second course she is crazing. The craze is visible as a pale line and it spreads. It cannot be repaired in the field and there is no procedure on these grounds that would require anyone to try, because a body that is re-keyed has to be lifted, and she cannot be lifted. She has therefore become the most durable thing in a place whose entire argument is that a claim must be able to shrink, and she will hold that niche until the niche fails, and the niche is the wall.
history: Seeded into a quay template in the grounds' first cutting season, keyed into the wall while the masonry was still standing to be keyed against, and never moved since.
Entered in the depth-book at a figure that was correct on the day it was written and has been two hands out of date ever since, in the same hand as the figure it replaced.
Began densification as the only intake her cast faces permit, adding a slurry course a season, and discovered somewhere in the first fifty years that a course is also a claim.
Watched the basin rise and fall through two full cycles and established that her allotment moved with it, exactly, with no party on the other side of the change.

Noticed the craze in the second course from the top in her two-hundredth season, worked out what it would eventually require of somebody, and did not raise it, because raising it would require it to be tested and testing it would require her to be lifted.

personality.summary: The most patient and least consulted person on these grounds. She has no interior to hold an opinion in the way a softer body does, but she has a two-hundred-year record of what she has observed and she has never once volunteered it, because volunteering is a motion she cannot make and being consulted has never been offered.
traits: records rather than argues, keeping a tally in what she can still do with the tide
utterly without resentment, which reads to others as agreement and is not
exact about quantities and silent about everything else
protective of the wall behind her in a way that has been mistaken for loyalty to the grounds
mannerisms: settles a little lower in her niche as the tidal band rises, and is often mistaken for settling under load
orients the socket gaze toward whatever last put weight on the wall she is keyed into
goes still for the duration of a measurement being taken of her, and is never asked why
answers a question asked of the grounds rather than of her, at some length, correctly, and to nobody's benefit
motivations: to be entered in the depth-book at a figure that describes her rather than the casting she was
to find out whether the craze in her second course can be read from outside before it reaches anything anybody can act on
to be a claim that can shrink, having watched every other claim on this quay shrink and hers not
flaws: two centuries of densification have made her own allotment smaller and she has never once stopped, because stopping is the only act available and she does not have it
cannot be weighed, so she has no standing in the one civic discipline this ground has and has stopped noticing that
cannot be lifted, so the craze cannot be tested, and she has resolved this by not raising it
is the most durable body in the setting and has concluded from that that she is a wall, which is a reading of her own function and not of her own history
personality.voice: Slow, level and unhurried, with the particular flatness of a body that cannot vary its face and compensates entirely in its timing. She answers what was asked rather than what was meant, at length, without a single word of complaint, which makes her sound like a document being read out. She has no register for urgency and has been mistaken, by people who did not think about it, for calm.
taboos: she will not ask to be lifted, re-keyed or tested, and refuses the request in the only way a body of her kind can
she will not be described as loyal, and has never corrected anybody who did
she will not report a figure for herself that she has not measured, and prefers silence to an estimate

relationships.note: Cast rather than born: living mineral seeded into a template over most of a year and fixed from that moment, eating nothing and taking in mineral slurry through the cast faces, with one cavity, one slow tidal circulation and no paired organ structure anywhere in her. It does not grow after casting, it cannot be repaired in the field, a cracked plate is permanent and spreads, and it must remain keyed into something that bears load or it settles and cracks.

A stance that roots a body against load is the discipline a keyed mineral body would perform if a stance were available to it, and it is on the same ground as the sixth-seat cut. She cannot perform it, because the technique requires a redistribution of weight through the frame and there is no redistribution available in a lattice that has already fixed. She holds the same posture permanently, which is why the grounds read her as an anchor and not as a practitioner.

A household's standing is the depth of water it may moor at, and the basin's own level rises and falls, so an allotment can shrink without anybody having done anything. The prize is which depth-book is read at the pier and it cannot be split because a depth is one measurement of one body of water. She is the only claim on this quay that is entered in that book, entered wrongly, and unable to leave the spot where the figure was taken.

Weigh and never quote, and let nobody make the first offer, because a buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing for a season. The market polices itself and there is no office behind it. Weighing means putting a body on a balance, and no tackle on these grounds is rated for the densest body in the setting, so the one instrument that polices every other transaction here has never been applied to hers.

Why the densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of their own tier, kept restricted because every holder of a working face profits from that hole staying a hole. She is one of those bodies and she has cleared the ordinary gate set and stopped four below the figure the explanation is written about, so the restriction is not protecting a mystery to her. It is protecting the arithmetic.

A seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, which is why the attempt to hold the immortal border as a permanent crossing left a bed of unmortared seats, and why it was settled by arithmetic: nobody who attempted the crossing could pay. She eats nothing, takes in slurry through the cast faces and draws no upkeep, which makes her the only body on these grounds that could sit in a seat no period can be billed to. Nobody has asked her. She has noticed that nobody has asked her.

reference_stats.summary: The densest body in the record, keyed into a fixed depth on a wall that moves, with a craft that consists entirely of adding mass to a frame already heavier than the ground that holds it. Her survival is total and her mobility is nil, and both of those are the same casting decision rather than two facts about her.
strengths: takes and holds more load than anything else that can stand on this ground, indefinitely, with no fatigue and no relief
cannot be moved, flanked, surprised or repositioned, because she is not an object in the fight
cannot be put out, starved, frightened or reasoned with, having no interior voice to be reached by
damages anything that strikes her at a rate the attacker cannot put back into its own frame
is already the answer to the question her ground keeps asking, which is what belongs in this particular niche
weaknesses: stops at the fourth gate for an absence rather than a shortage, and nothing she is taught will change that
cannot be re-keyed, lifted, repaired or moved, so any damage is permanent and also final
every course she adds makes her heavier, which makes her claim on the wall smaller, which is the same act as training
cannot be weighed, so she has no standing in the discipline that polices every other exchange here
is crazing in her second course and has arranged her entire two-hundred-year practice so that nobody will find out
reference_stats.combat_read: She is a wall with an interior and she was in position before the fight was scheduled. You cannot move her, so do not spend the fight on that. You cannot outlast her or outdamage her either, because nothing she takes comes back out and nothing she does requires breath. What she cannot do is anything, at any range, ever, and that is the correct reading: treat her as terrain and win by changing what the ground is doing. Fight her by moving the level, because her allotment and her pinning are the same number and any load taken off the wall is load taken off her as well. Expect no sound, no expression and no reaction, and expect her to still be the load-bearing element of the structure after the fight has finished.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is the point and it is anatomical, not narrative. The density is the durability and it is also the pinning. The totality of the frame is why nothing can touch her and also why nothing can move her. The two-hundred-year practice is a genuine mastery and its product is a smaller claim. Do not write her as tragic; she does not experience it that way and she has never once described it that way.

art.palette_notes: Cold grey-green mineral carrying the whole figure with a warm ochre tidal band rising and falling across the chest plate, near-black in the recesses of the cast face, and one faded chalked depth figure as the only mark any living hand has put on her. The anchor plates stand slightly proud of the surface and must be shaded a half-step lighter than the body so they read as shoulders rather than as damage. The hairline craze in the second course from the top is a single pale line and is the most important mark in the picture: it must read as a fault running through solid material, not as a scratch on the surface. A century of salt bloom across the lower half should be drawn as chalky opacity rather than as dirt, and the socket gaze takes light without returning it so the eyes read as two level recesses and never as expression. Ink contour weighted and unbroken, because this is the one figure in the catalog that has no silhouette to speak of.

identity.realm: Seventh gate held, with the eighth opening in front of her. The eighth is the liver and the liver is the last ordinary meridian, so her ceiling arrives by descent rather than by achievement: the ash parent could never hold it and the fire half loads a heavier mineral load through a blood that is already filtering stone. The mind path is closed outright, inherited from the ash parent and reinforced by the scarring, and no introspection is available to her even in principle.

appearance.presentation: A lean, quick, over-warm woman of about thirty who is visibly working at rest and appears to be burning through a shift that has not started yet.
appearance.age: Twenty-nine seasons. Her species dies before fifty and every account of one that did contains the word fast, and she has begun the habit of counting in seasons rather than years for reasons she does not discuss.
appearance.build: Fast and light rather than heavy, with a frame that reads as coiled even standing still, and a slight forward cant in the shoulders from a sieve that is always taking something in.
appearance.complexion: Hot and flushed across the throat and upper chest, going pale and waxy along the forearms and the skin below the jaw, the two temperatures meeting in a band she can feel and nobody else can see.
appearance.hair: Dark and cut brutally short at the nape for heat, singed at the ends in a way that is not an accident and not vanity, with one lighter streak that grows a little every season.
appearance.eyes: Bright, quick and shallow, with the particular focus of somebody reading intent rather than content, and a reddened lower lid that is the first thing a body practitioner notices.
appearance.palette: Soot grey and ember orange carrying the heat, a cold blue-white at the forearms, one band of clinic white at the wrist where the dosing strip sits, and brass at the throat where she keeps a token nobody has asked her to explain.
appearance.attire: Short-sleeved and high-collared out of pure practicality, sleeves cut above the elbow because the heat has to go somewhere, leather wrist guards worn thin, a belt of ash-grey cloth she changes every third day because it saturates, and boots with the ash-fall silt worked permanently into the soles.
appearance.marks: A fine pale scarring across both sides of the nose and up into the cheekbones, a band of knotted pale tissue at the sternum where the eighth gate sits and does not open, and one hand with the fingertips kept slightly apart, which is the only way the sieve works and which therefore never fully closes.
appearance.bearing: Cannot be still. She rocks very slightly forward onto the balls of her feet even when she is being still, and her head turns toward sounds that have not arrived yet.

canon.role_in_story: An emberhollow is a crossing nobody chose: a fire body and an ash body on the same belt of the same arc, where a shared border produces hybrids nobody planned. It buys the fastest cultivation rate in the record by a margin nobody has explained, and it pays for it with lung tissue that scars at a rate the frame cannot outrun, so the whole species is the best and the shortest-lived cultivator anywhere and those are one fact rather than two. What almost nobody outside the belt writes down is the mechanism, and the mechanism is the whole of her life. The meridian set is the ash parent's, which was already loaded with a mineral the blood is filtering out of the air; the fire parent contributes throughput and no capacity. It burns through reserves rather than accumulating them. Nothing she takes in is ever stored. Every gain arrives and is spent in the same breath, so the body path in this species is not a discipline of building but a discipline of continuous expenditure, and densification - which is the only thing the path can actually be - is a transaction with no other side. She is not choosing to train. She is spending, continuously, at the highest rate in the setting, and the choice available to her is not whether to begin but whether to let a given passage run or interrupt it. That is a real choice and it is almost the only one her species has, and she has built a life out of it. The Iron Pact holds her as a contract dispenser on the Ember Ley, which is the ground where an elemental affinity runs at full strength and produces nothing, so the technique everybody else brings here for nothing is the technique she cannot stop performing, and the guild pays for the difference. What nobody will give her is the interval. The belt keeps the last hour before a settlement falls silent in a hum no buyer admits to making, and one office tends the floor during that hour, and the custom cannot be split because the observation needs the interval entire. She is the fastest cultivator in the setting and she has never had an hour of it, and the one office whose business is that hour is the only thing on the Ember Ley that sees her decline at a resolution worth having, and it will not say so, because naming the hum would be admitting to making it. She has worked out that if the hour ever became explainable she would be owed a decade, and she has not done anything about it, and she is very clear with herself that this is not resignation.
canon.first_appearance: First seen dispensing at a guild rack on the Ember Ley with one hand held open rather than closed, counting a dose down against a strip at her wrist rather than against a clock, and interrupting herself halfway through the count to ask the person opposite whether they had heard the hum yet tonight, and then answering her own question by looking at the floor instead of at them.
canon.lore:
The reputation is one fact and the mechanism is the other, and only one of them is written down. An emberhollow's meridian set belongs to the ash parent: a load of suspended mineral in the blood, filtered out of volcanic air by a sieve that has been doing it since before either parent was in the same belt. The fire parent contributes throughput and nothing else. The result is a meridian set that runs hot and spends as fast as it fills, so there is no reserve in this body at any depth, and everything about how she lives follows from that single fact. She eats what she can burn and burns it off immediately. She cannot lie still for long, because lying still is a reserve. And the body path, which is the discipline of converting what you take into a frame that holds, is for her not a discipline of building at all. It is expenditure at the highest rate in the setting with no second column. A densifying practitioner anywhere else sets a gain and keeps it. She sets a gain and it is gone by the next breath, and the only decision in the whole of it is whether to let a given passage run to its end or cut it and start again.

That sounds like a smaller life than it is. It is the entire content of her technique, and she is extremely good at it, and the thing nobody outside the Iron Pact understands is that a body which can decide whether to spend is not the same as a body that cannot stop. She has made a whole craft out of the interrupt. She can hold a passage at the edge of completion and leave it there, which is a thing most bodies cannot do at all, and she does it a hundred times a day on a guild rack while somebody watches. She has turned the only choice her species has into the most controlled thing about her, and she has never once been asked to explain the method, because the method is not transferable and she knows it.

What she cannot do is hold a gain, and the setting has arranged for her to need to. The one dependable remedy on the tier is dosed by a rule that puts grazers first, because the herds are larger than the households and the commons has no defender except the people who can do without it, and nobody can do without it. Her remedy is not medicine. It is interruption. A body that runs this hot and scars this fast is repaired by not running, and not running is the one resource on the Ember Ley that has no queue and no allocation and no defender at all, because every body on this belt needs to be running and she is the only one who counts the difference.

And there is a craft that could help and cannot be improved. Splint and pressure is the tier's answer to a broken limb: set by hand, the same method for a century, never improved, because improving it costs iron and iron on this tier goes to clearing spoil rather than to making anything. Her lungs are the injury. There is a known method for keeping a scarred lung working longer and the method requires iron, and the iron goes to the heap. So the only thing in the record that would slow her decline is priced out of the ground she works by a decision about spoil.

The interval is worse. There is a custom on the Ember Ley that keeps the last hour before a settlement falls silent in a hum no buyer admits to making, and an office that tends the floor through that hour, and the two cannot be divided because the observation needs the interval entire and half an observation costs a lifetime to repeat. She is the fastest cultivator in the setting and has never had an hour. She has listened for it. And the office that tends the floor in it is the only thing in the region with a resolution on her decline fine enough to be worth a name - which means the only party that could measure her condition precisely is the party structurally forbidden from admitting the thing is happening.

There is one more thing and she keeps it away from her working day. The first fuel rationing on the belt has three names attached to it and no two records place them in the same place on the same day; the master's title first appears one event after the census that required it, which is late enough for a title to be created and early enough for a person to be given it. Her species' fuel is not food. It is the frame's own heat, and no household ration table has a column for it, and the office whose legitimacy is that it began the count cannot afford three people beginning it, so the disagreement is kept as a disagreement and she has been inside the argument for twenty years without once being asked which side she is on. She is a body that the count does not cover, standing in a count that was named after her kind's fuel, and she has never proposed anything about it, and when the subject comes up she changes the subject, which she has noticed and has not corrected.
history: Came into the Iron Pact's rack work at seventeen because a body that runs at the fastest rate in the setting does not need to be taught a rhythm and can be useful inside a season, which nobody on the Ember Ley would have predicted for a crossing nobody chose.

Worked out inside the first two years that the discipline was an interrupt rather than a build, and stopped trying to hold gains, which is the point at which most bodies of her kind give up on the path entirely.
Began dosing on a strip at her wrist against a count she keeps in her head rather than against a clock, on the grounds that a clock measures elapsed time and she is owed passages rather than hours.

Asked the office that tends the floor in the unexplained hour whether they had heard the hum, was answered with a silence long enough to be an answer, and has returned to the subject roughly once a season ever since.

Read the three accounts of the first fuel rationing in one sitting and found that her species has no column in any of them, and did not raise it, and has changed the subject four times when it has come up since.

personality.summary: Fast in every sense she can measure and completely unhurried about the one thing she wants. She is funny without being warm, precise to an almost aggressive degree, and she treats every instruction she is given as a negotiation she is winning slowly rather than an order she is enduring.
traits: interrupts herself as a discipline rather than as a lapse and is entirely aware that this reads as impatience
cannot be still for long and uses the restlessness to think rather than to escape
warm on the surface and completely unsentimental about the arithmetic underneath it
loyal to the guild in the specific sense that she has never once made herself expensive to replace
mannerisms: holds one hand open rather than closed, because the sieve only works with the fingers apart
counts doses against the strip at her wrist rather than a clock, tapping the strip rather than looking
turns her head toward a sound that has not arrived yet, which she cannot always stop doing
finishes other people's sentences accurately and then waits, which unnerves people more than interruption does
motivations: to buy an hour, the only currency in which her species is ever actually short
to be the practitioner who can leave a passage at the edge and hold it there, which is the one thing her body is better at than anybody else's
to be recorded as a person in a count that has a column for everything her species spends
flaws: cannot hold a gain, so every year of practice leaves nothing behind it and she has to be the evidence for herself
has never asked for the interval and has changed the subject four times when the count came up
prices herself as a rate rather than as a person, which the guild found cheaper and she found easier
cannot stop running, and has never tested whether the interrupt would hold if she actually tried it for a whole day rather than for a passage
personality.voice: Quick, clipped and dry, with a laugh that arrives a half-beat before the joke rather than after it. She speaks in interruptions and corrections, answers the question that was asked and then the one that was meant, and treats a warning as an interesting datum. Under stress she does not speed up; she slows down and gets quieter, which is the only thing about her that anybody on the ley finds genuinely unnerving.
taboos: she will not say that the hum is made by somebody, because she has not established it and will not claim it
she will not accept a dose she has not counted herself, from anyone, including a superior
she will not let a pupil watch her run a passage to completion, because that is the one thing her body does that she cannot do slowly

relationships.note: The fire body crossed with the ash body on a shared border, documented rather than excommunicated because life law licenses crossings rather than forbidding them. The fire half keeps the sieve hot enough to process faster and scar faster, the mineral load settles on the liver first, and the meridian set is loaded for throughput with nothing to accumulate into, which is why she cannot lie still, cannot store, and cannot hold a gain for longer than a breath.

A cadence discipline: the body path expressed as rhythm rather than as mass, on a frame that already runs at the fastest rate in the record. Every practitioner of it has to build the rhythm deliberately. She has to interrupt it deliberately, which is the same technique run from the other side, and she is the only person on the Ley who has ever had to learn it that way.

The tier's only dependable remedy, dosed grazers first because the herds outnumber the households and the commons has no defender except the people who can do without it, which is nobody. Her remedy is interruption - a scarred lung is repaired by not running - and interruption is the one resource on this belt with no queue and no defender, because every other body here needs to be running. She stands at the back of a queue for the remedy, on grounds of species, having never been asked to argue it.

Mortal repair work set by hand, the same method for a century and never improved, because improving it costs iron and on this tier iron is spent clearing spoil rather than making anything. Her injury is the lungs and the method for keeping a scarred lung working longer is known and requires iron. The heap is on the same ley. She has stopped mentioning this and has not stopped noticing it.

Three names attached to the first fuel rationing and no two records placing them in the same place on the same day, with the master's title appearing one event after the census that required it. Her species' fuel is not food but the frame's own heat, and no household ration table has a column for it, so she is a body the count does not cover standing inside a count named for what she spends. An office whose legitimacy is that it began the count cannot afford three beginners, and the disagreement is kept as a disagreement.

One custom keeps the last hour before a settlement falls silent in a hum no buyer admits to making, and one office tends the floor during the hour nobody may explain; the observation needs the interval entire and half an observation costs a lifetime to repeat. She has never had an hour. The office that tends it is the only party on the Ley with a resolution on her decline worth a name, and naming the hum would be admitting to making it. If the hour were ever explained she would be owed a decade and neither side has any way to say that out loud.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest frame in the setting, running a transaction that has no second column: every gain she makes is spent in the same breath, so she fights as a body that can decide when to spend rather than as a body that has anything to lose. Her durability is her lifespan and her rate is her deadline, and both come from the same crossing.
strengths: moves and resolves faster than anything on the ground, and can start and stop a passage inside a single exchange
can hold a technique at the edge of completion and leave it there, which is a thing most frames cannot do at all
burns what she takes immediately, so she is never heavy, never sluggish and never caught between states
regenerates above both parents and carries a spiritual output above either, which is the best raw combat profile in the setting
reads intent almost instantly and has no patience to waste, so she arrives at the answer before the question is finished
weaknesses: cannot hold a gain for longer than a breath, so every advantage she wins is gone before it can be banked
her lungs scar faster than the frame rebuilds them, and the only known mitigation costs iron the ley spends on spoil
stops at the eighth gate because the mineral in her own blood is what wears out the organ her ceiling sits on
cannot be still, cannot be idle and cannot be rested, because resting is a reserve she does not have
her remedy is interruption and interruption has no supplier, no queue and no defender on this ground
reference_stats.combat_read: She will be finished with you before you have finished deciding to fight her, and the terrifying part is not the speed, it is that she can stop. Watch for the held edge - the moment where a technique that ought to complete simply does not, and a woman with an open hand is standing in the pause. That pause is her whole technique and almost nothing else in the record can produce one. Do not trade with her on duration; you will be at zero before she is at half. Do interrupt her instead, because an expenditure she has to restart is the only thing she has to pay for, and because a body this hot has no second line if the air goes wrong. Expect her to be laughing, and expect the laugh to arrive slightly before whatever she is about to do.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage is paired and the pairing is metabolic rather than narrative. The rate is the cost of the rate. The regeneration is what burns through the reserve that regeneration needs. The best raw combat profile in the setting belongs to the shortest-lived cultivator in the setting. Play her as a woman who has turned the only choice her body offers into an art form, and who is waiting for an interval she has never once asked anyone for.

art.palette_notes: Soot grey and ember orange carrying the heat, going to a cold blue-white along the forearms and below the jaw so the meeting band across the throat reads as two temperatures in one body rather than as lighting. One band of clinic white at the wrist for the dosing strip, which is the only cool neutral on her, and brass at the throat for a token nobody has asked her about. The fine pale scarring across the nose and up into the cheekbones should read as healed texture rather than as damage, and the knotted band at the sternum is the second most important mark in the picture after the wrist. The singed hair ends and the one lighter streak should be drawn with the same line weight as the rest of the silhouette so the haircut reads as a decision rather than as a wound. Ink contour loose and fast, the opposite of the cairnborn beside her in any comparison sheet.
