identity.realm: Ordinal four, and the fourth gate is the yin-organ gate. It is inherited from the mineral parent unchanged, because heat is not a second organ: he has one cavity with a working fire circulation in it and no paired organ set to run a channel between. He is the most durable body anyone can build and it has bought him one quarter of the ladder on a span of about sixty years.

appearance.presentation: A man of about fifty who could pass for thirty from the shoulders down and could not pass for anything at all from the neck up, standing like something that has been leaned against for a long time.
appearance.age: Fifty-one seasons against a span of about sixty, which he refers to in his own ledgers as remainder and which everyone around him has politely agreed not to calculate.
appearance.build: Denser than either parent and heavier than anything else on the plain, with a mineral frame showing through the skin at the jaw, the knuckles and the collarbone as a cold grey-green, and a genuine fire circulation running hot enough to be felt through clothing at a distance of a hand's width.
appearance.complexion: Two textures in one body: dead-cool mineral grey along the jaw and the backs of the hands, live and flushed everywhere else, with the boundary sitting exactly at the top of the sternum and moving very slightly from day to day.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, cropped at the back where the mineral comes closest, and standing slightly away from the skull as though the frame were running warmer than the air around it.
appearance.eyes: Pale, level and unhurried, set in mineral that takes light flatly, and they track a structure rather than a face - he is reading the ground behind whoever he is looking at.
appearance.palette: Quarry grey and cold slate carrying the figure, ember red from the throat down and visible at the open collar, a hard white at the knuckles where the lattice comes through, and one worn leather band at the right wrist that has no buckle and no ornament.
appearance.attire: Heavy and close-fitted out of necessity rather than fashion, because loose cloth on a body this hot is a scorch risk; a sleeveless outer coat worn open, a high collar turned down and fastened, gloves at the belt unused because nobody has yet shown him that they would survive contact with him.
appearance.marks: The cold mineral lattice showing through at the jaw and the backs of both hands, a pale seam of older crazing at the right shoulder that has been there long enough to be a landmark, and an old burn-scar on the inside of one wrist where a hand he was teaching once held on for too long.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried and slightly downhill-weighed, the feet set wider than a soft body needs and the shoulders squared to whatever structure is nearest, so that he is never standing with his back to a load path even in a doorway.

canon.role_in_story: A stonebound is one recorded crossing of a mineral body with a fire body, kept and named as a line rather than noted as an oddity. The mineral half does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be extinguished, so a stonebound killed properly stays dead and one injured stays injured; the frame outlasts the fire parent's lifespan by a factor of two and the whole life is about sixty years, and those are the same fact. The frame is a mineral lattice carrying a genuine fire circulation instead of the tidal one, hot to the touch, denser than either parent, and visibly a compromise, because the organ pairs are still not there. Kereth holds the Spoilwright's heap account, and that office has no term in it. It is not an office that can be declared vacant, because declaring a vacancy requires a procedure to certify the post empty, and the procedure reads the post's own continuity rather than the occupant's; what it actually reads is the frame. He is the account. He is also the only person on the plain who is not going anywhere, in the most literal sense available on ground where waste does not disperse and forty years of heap still stands on ore that is gone. The Spoilwright does not pay him, because there is nothing to pay and he does not consume. It files him instead, and the filing is what makes him hard to remove. And here is the arrangement that governs his entire life. His soul is seated high in the frame and it is durable in a way neither parent's soul is: it survives his body's death more reliably than his body survives anything at all. So the one procedure that would empty the post - kill him properly, which is reliable against the frame and is the only method the record has - removes the occupant and not the office. Every sworn member of the guild who holds no office is filed as a Ward, and recognition begins exactly where office begins, so the moment his body stops being him his post becomes a Ward with a durable holder in it rather than a vacancy with a body in the way. He has read that arrangement. He has been waiting at the eighth gate of a ladder he cannot climb for eleven years in order not to reach it early, and he has never once told anybody why, and he has told exactly one person.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on the heap with his hand flat on the standing barrow, head turned away from the man he was speaking to and toward the face behind him, answering a question about the account by naming a course that had begun to take load, and being told by the man he was speaking to that he had asked about the account, not about the face.
canon.lore:
Start with the frame, because everything else about him is downstream of it. The mineral half does not regenerate. The fire half cannot be put out. Between them they produce the densest, hardest, most durable body in the record and they also produce a span of about sixty years, and those are the same statement rather than a good thing and a bad thing: the durability belongs to a mineral lattice and the lifespan belongs to a fire, and one of them runs out long before the other. A stonebound killed properly stays dead. A stonebound injured stays injured, forever, with no exception that any technique in the record has ever produced. His interior is the compromise the crossing literally is - one cavity carrying a real circulation where a tidal one used to be, hot to the touch, no paired organ structure anywhere in it - so he clears the ordinary gate set and stops at the fourth, and heat is not a second organ no matter how much heat there is.

The part that governs his life is not in that paragraph. It is that his soul is seated high in the frame and is more durable than either parent's, and that it survives his body's death more reliably than his body survives anything. On most bodies that would be a line in a record and not a fact in a life. On his it is the whole of his employment. The Spoilwright exists because spatial law is unspent on this plain, so waste does not disperse and the heap has to be carried out by hand before the face can advance. That makes the containment holding the heap off the face the one irreplaceable asset the guild has, and the containment is him. There is no term in the office, because the office's continuity is measured by the frame rather than by the man, and the frame is rated for longer than the man has. Every sworn member who holds no office is filed as a Ward instead, and the guild's protection stops and the sect's recognition begins in exactly the same place, so an emptied post does not become available. It becomes a Ward post with a durable holder in it.

And the one procedure that would empty it does not. Kill him properly and the frame stops, which the record guarantees and which has never once been in doubt. What is not in doubt anywhere in the record is whether the soul stops with it, and his is the frame's own argument against the assumption: it sits high, it is more durable than either parent's, and it outlasts his body. So the method is reliable about the frame and silent about everything the guild actually needs. He worked that out in his second decade of holding the account and has spent the two decades since arranging his own life around it.

His path is the body path, which is complete in his species and is the entire point of the line. It is also, for him, the exact process that closes the arrangement on itself. The body discipline densifies: it converts what is taken into a frame that holds more, and the craft that does it most efficiently on a mineral frame is the tempered frame, which is a dual-path technique because it needs qi and body together and a frame that can conduct both without tearing. He is extremely good at it. It is the only technique in the record he can perform to completion, because everything about him was built to hold, and each course he adds makes him a better container. Which is the point, from the guild's side and not from his: a better container needs its contents less urgently. He has understood that his ascent is a straight line toward being unnecessary, and he has not stopped, because stopping is the one act this body cannot perform and because he has nowhere to put the years if he does.

There is a second thing the frame of his kind has done to somebody. The setting's only durable library keeps its archive in one body turning over at about a percent a year and living four centuries, and it cannot take the body path at all, because hardening the bone stops the turnover the memory runs on. So the one body in the setting that can hold a record for four hundred years is the one body that must never be hardened - and he is the body that has been hardening for thirty years. He has looked at that pair of facts more than once. He is the only frame in the setting that would end the only memory in it, and the arithmetic of that is not complicated and he has not acted on it, and he has never told anyone he had done the arithmetic.

What he has done is keep a ledger, which is the one thing his species is bad at. Not a count of haulage. A count of years, kept the way a culture whose whole practice is that a count is never an estimate would keep it, entry by entry, on the grounds that the only exact record on this side of the peaks summarises sixty years instead of writing them down and that a filled gap would be an admission. His span is about sixty. The gap is his own length. He is not filling it. He is making sure that when somebody eventually asks what happened in the years nobody wrote down, there is a set of figures in his hand rather than a silence with his body in it, and he is the only person alive who will still be there when the question gets asked, and that is the reason he has not spent the years trying to buy a seat he cannot hold.
history: Inherited the heap account on his thirtieth season, at which point the office had been held by four men and by nothing else, and the appointment was made by a guild that had run out of candidates rather than by anybody choosing him.

Established inside a decade that the account's continuity was read off the frame and not off him, and that the only procedure which emptied it did not empty the office, and told exactly one person, who has been dead for six seasons.

Began the tempered frame at thirty-five and discovered that he was the only practitioner on the plain who could complete it, because every other frame either tore under it or could not hold the load long enough to finish.
Read the library's practice and worked out that a body of his kind, hardened, would end the only durable memory in the setting, and did not tell the library, and did not stop.

Started his own year count entry by entry in the year the guild first summarised sixty instead of writing it, on the grounds that a filled gap would be an admission and he would rather be the source of the figure than the reason it was needed.

personality.summary: The most patient man in the setting and the most economical with himself. He does not waste words, does not repeat himself, and has arranged his entire life around a single administrative fact with the same lack of drama a man brings to a leaking roof.
traits: reads a load or a face out of the same sense and does not distinguish them in conversation
quietly funny on a long cycle, roughly four times a season, and never once at anybody's expense
unsentimental about his own span in a way that other people find either admirable or offensive
given to acting on arrangements rather than on people, and aware of the difference
mannerisms: turns his head toward the nearest structure before he answers a question about a person
sets his feet wider than the ground requires and never once shifts them while talking
puts his palm flat against whatever he is standing next to, the way a person checks a wall
answers questions about the account by answering questions about the face behind him, and does not apologise for it
motivations: to be the source of the sixty years rather than the reason the figures were ever needed
to hold the account until it is taken from him by somebody who can be shown the arrangement
to keep the guild's protection and the sect's recognition from landing on the same vacancy at the same time
flaws: cannot stop practising, so he is steadily becoming the thing his office does not need
has told nobody for eleven years why he will not open the last gate he is actually able to open
refuses help in a way that has cost him two hands' worth of other people's time and his own
would rather be a durable vacancy than a living man with a term, and has not examined that preference
personality.voice: Low, level and unhurried, with the flatness of a man who expects to still be having this conversation in twenty years and has no reason to raise his voice before then. He answers the question asked and does not volunteer, and when he does volunteer it is a fact with a date on it. He has one joke and it is about paperwork.
taboos: he will not accept a term, an expiry or a relief, and treats the offer as an insult to the arrangement rather than as a kindness to himself
he will not let anyone train him and does not explain why
he will not write down a year he has not lived through, which has cost him the last eleven entries

relationships.note: A mineral lattice carrying a genuine fire circulation instead of a tidal one, hot to the touch, denser than either parent, visibly a compromise. The mineral half does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be extinguished, so injury is permanent and a proper killing is permanent, and the frame outlasts the fire parent's lifespan by a factor of two while the whole life remains about sixty. Those are the same fact and they are the whole reason the line was kept.

A dual-path technique because it needs qi and body together and a frame that will conduct both without tearing. It is the only technique in the record he can carry to completion: every softer frame either tears under it or cannot hold the load long enough to finish. On him it works beautifully, and what it produces is a denser, better-insulated occupant, which is precisely the outcome his guild would prefer to need him for.

Bodies holding more life than their frame can inscribe reach the twenty-ninth gate and none has ever come back to describe the thirtieth, so the question is not what is past it but whether past it is a gate or the end of the ladder - and the answer is expensive for anybody whose authority depends on the ladder visibly stopping somewhere. His soul is seated high in the frame and is more durable than either parent's. He is the literal case, and the ladder he cannot climb past the fourth is the ladder the whole reading rests on.

The only exact record below the spirit peaks carries sixty years as a summary instead of entry by entry, in a culture whose whole practice is that a count is never an estimate; a filled gap would be an admission. His span is about sixty. He has kept his own year count entry by entry for twenty-nine seasons precisely so that the gap will have a source rather than a silence, and he is the only person who will still be standing when the question is finally asked.

The only durable library keeps its archive in one body turning over at about a percent a year across four centuries, and it cannot take the body path because hardening the bone stops the turnover the memory runs on. So the one frame that could hold a record for four hundred years is the frame that must never be hardened, and he has been hardening for thirty years. He has done the arithmetic. He has told the library nothing, and he goes and stands in the reading hall twice a season.

Every sworn member who holds no office is a Ward and every sworn member of the sect who holds no office sits at the open door; the house's protection ends where the sect's recognition begins, in exactly the same place. Kill him properly and the frame stops, which is reliable, while his soul outlives the frame rather than stopping with it. An emptied post therefore does not become available for anyone. It becomes a Ward post with a holder who cannot be replaced by killing him.

reference_stats.summary: The most durable body in the setting, held on a span of about sixty years, with a soul that outlives the frame rather than stopping with it. He fights as the ground: nothing he takes comes back out, nothing he does requires breath, and every course he completes makes him a slightly worse reason to keep fighting.
strengths: takes weight at a point where it is arriving and converts it, so his frame improves inside other people's emergencies and nowhere else
feels a structure about to fail before it does, through the lattice, at a resolution no crew instrument reaches
absorbs damage permanently rather than temporarily, so a fight he has already survived cannot be won the same way twice
burns what he takes immediately, so he is never heavy and never caught between states
needs no rotation and no relief, which makes him the cheapest way to keep dangerous ground open
weaknesses: stops at the fourth gate for an absence rather than a shortage, and heat is not a second organ however much of it there is
every injury is permanent and nothing closes one, so a bad call costs him for the rest of his life
dies at about sixty regardless of how well anything is going, and the whole of his life is the first part of that
cannot be put out, so he must eat constantly and his availability is a supply question before it is a virtue
cannot be relieved, so there is no point in the fight at which anybody may successfully stop being afraid of him
reference_stats.combat_read: He will be standing in the worst place on the ground when the fight starts, because that is where the load is, and he will have been there before you knew the fight was happening. You cannot move him, flank him or outlast him, and every blow you land is stored permanently in a frame that will still be carrying it in a decade, so do not spend the fight hurting him. Make the ground move instead: a body that takes weight off a structure has to be argued with by the structure, and he is the only thing holding it up. He is also the only body in the setting whose attention goes to a building rather than to you, so the only thing that reliably brings it onto you is standing between him and a load path. Expect him to be slow, hot, and completely unbothered, and expect him to be the last one still there, for a reason that has nothing to do with the fight.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is the entire design of the species and none of it is narrative. The durability is bought with the span. The healing is absent because the mineral half does not regenerate. The fire that will not go out is what requires him to eat constantly. And the persistence that makes his office unevictable is the same persistence that means killing him does not empty it. Play him as a man who is patiently making himself unnecessary and is the only person in the setting who knows it.

art.palette_notes: Quarry grey and cold slate carrying the figure, ember red from the throat down and clearly visible at the open collar so the heat in him reads as internal rather than as costume, with a hard white at the knuckles and jaw where the mineral lattice comes through the skin and takes light flatly. The boundary between the two temperatures must sit exactly at the top of the sternum and must be the single cleanest edge in the picture, because it is the visible compromise the whole species is. One worn unadorned leather band at the right wrist is the only object on him with no function, and the old burn scar inside that wrist must be drawn at the same weight as the lattice and not softer. Ink contour heavy and slightly broken across the old shoulder seam, the way masonry cracks.
